###### Notes

Estimates here may not match other sources due to enrollment categorization differences and differences in measures of Medicaid spending. The spending data used in these estimates are from Medicaid claims which reflect spending at the time health care services are used or premium payments are made, whereas other measures of spending may reflect the timing of state payments to providers. Additionally, estimates here do not include prescription drug rebates and most supplemental payments to providers, which other Medicaid spending sources may include.

A small number of Medicaid enrollees whose eligibility group is unknown are not broken out into a separate column but are included in state and national totals.

States with "Unusable" data quality according to the CMS DQ Atlas indicators "Medicaid-Only Enrollment", "Eligibility Group Code", "Age" and "Medicaid Beneficiary Expenditures" are not included in these tables and are not included in national totals. For more information on data quality issues that may lead to unusual spending or enrollment, see CMS DQ Atlas. Caution is recommended when comparing data between years since different states may be included in each year due to data quality.

###### Sources

KFF analysis of the T-MSIS Research Identifiable Files, 2023 (Preliminary)

**N/A:** Not Applicable. These states had not adopted the ACA Medicaid expansion as of the reporting year.

**NSD:** Not Significant Data. Due to data security measures, the values of cells with fewer than 50 enrollees are not reported but are included in state and national totals.

**DQ:** Data Quality. Data categorized as "Unusable" based on the DQ Atlas. These values are not included in the national totals, unless otherwise specified in a footnote.

**Enrollees:** Individuals who are enrolled in Medicaid at any time during the calendar year.

**Seniors:** Enrollees age 65 and older.

**People with Disabilities:** Enrollees under age 65 who are reported as eligible due to a disability.

**Adults:** Enrollees ages 19 to 64 who are not eligible due to a disability or newly eligible for Medicaid by the ACA Medicaid expansion.

**Children:** Enrollees ages 18 and younger who are not eligible due to a disability.

**ACA Expansion Adults:** Enrollees ages 19 to 64 who were made newly eligible for Medicaid by the ACA Medicaid expansion.

### Notes

Estimates here may not match other sources due to enrollment categorization differences and differences in measures of Medicaid spending. The spending data used in these estimates are from Medicaid claims which reflect spending at the time health care services are used or premium payments are made, whereas other measures of spending may reflect the timing of state payments to providers. Additionally, estimates here do not include prescription drug rebates and most supplemental payments to providers, which other Medicaid spending sources may include. A small number of Medicaid enrollees whose eligibility group is unknown are not broken out into a separate column but are included in state and national totals. States with "Unusable" data quality according to the CMS DQ Atlas indicators "Medicaid-Only Enrollment", "Eligibility Group Code", "Age" and "Medicaid Beneficiary Expenditures" are not included in these tables and are not included in national totals. For more information on data quality issues that may lead to unusual spending or enrollment, see CMS DQ Atlas. Caution is recommended when comparing data between years since different states may be included in each year due to data quality.
